chosen.premise: Rattata's incisors grow until death—and if they get too long, it cannot eat and starves.
chosen.hook: Rattata can starve because its teeth never stop growing.
chosen.visualIdea: A tooth-growth meter climbs as Rattata gnaws objects, ending with food blocked by overgrown incisors.
chosen.note: A genuinely unsettling contradiction: the survival tool Rattata needs can ultimately prevent it from eating. Multiple entries directly support the full premise.

candidates.premise: Seeing one Rattata means 40 more are certain to be living nearby.
candidates.hook: Spot one Rattata? There are 40 more nearby.
candidates.visualIdea: One Rattata freezes on screen, then the frame rapidly fills with 40 numbered silhouettes.
candidates.note: A highly specific canonical population rule, directly stated in two Pokédex entries and easy to visualize.

candidates.premise: Despite standing just 0.3 meters tall, Rattata's sharp incisors can cut right through hard wood.
candidates.hook: This 0.3-meter Pokémon can cut through hard wood.
candidates.visualIdea: A size ruler shows 0.3 m beside Rattata, then its bite slices dramatically through a hard wooden beam.
candidates.note: The 0.3-meter-versus-hardwood contrast is concrete and cinematic, but the source says its incisors can cut through hard wood without specifying the mechanics of a dramatic beam-cutting bite.

candidates.premise: Without something to file its ever-growing incisors, Rattata may chew door frames and table legs.
candidates.hook: A Rattata needs a file—or your furniture becomes the file.
candidates.visualIdea: Split screen: a file saves the teeth; no file leads to animated bite marks racing across a door and table.
candidates.note: Strong practical consequence with excellent visuals, but the house-destruction framing is narrower than the source, which specifically names door frames and table legs.

candidates.premise: Even while asleep, extremely cautious Rattata moves its ears constantly to listen for danger.
candidates.hook: Rattata is still on guard while it sleeps.
candidates.visualIdea: A sleeping Rattata fills the screen while exaggerated ear movements catch tiny danger-sound waves.
candidates.note: Well-supported and characterful, though the basic idea of a cautious animal staying alert during sleep is less startling than the tooth premise.

candidates.premise: Standard Rattata is Normal-type, but its Alolan variety becomes Dark/Normal and weighs 0.3 kg more.
candidates.hook: Alola turns Rattata from Normal into Dark/Normal.
candidates.visualIdea: Rattata slides through an Alola transition: type badge changes to Dark/Normal while weight ticks from 3.5 to 3.8 kg.
candidates.note: Accurate and cleanly supported, but type changes and a 0.3-kilogram weight increase are familiar regional-variant material and less emotionally compelling.
